claims.text: A machine-learning-based potential can improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation of liquid atomic configurations produces better reference–target phase-space overlap.
Using a machine-learning-based potential reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys at or near their high melting temperatures.
The proposed intervention is implementation of a machine-learning-based potential.
The proposed method is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic alloys.
The proposed method is applicable near the alloy melting point.
Complex interatomic interactions are the structural mediator relevant to reference quality.
A machine-learning potential learns patterns and trends from large datasets.
Learning patterns from large datasets allows a machine-learning potential to represent atomic configurations more accurately.
Improved phase-space overlap and reduced integration-path mismatch lead to more accurate predictions of high-entropy-alloy properties.
TOR-TILD uses EAM references as the baseline.
The applicable composition and temperature ranges are limited by the availability of training data and computational resources.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning potential depends on the quality and quantity of its training data.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning potential depends on implementation details.
Free energy of mixing or melting point can serve as the decisive free-energy benchmark for comparison with TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Failure to show a significant improvement in phase-space overlap and thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
